cases.reason: The goal names the change and its place (an Export CSV button on the Thimblevane admin Orders page), the details give the users, the four columns in order and the date-filter behaviour, and the criteria (button above the table, one row per shown order with those columns, only the filtered week's orders) can each be seen or checked.

The goal names the change and the place (Quillmoor members site reset links expire 30 minutes after sending), the details say what the expired-link page must show and what behaviour stays the same, and the criteria for opening a link at 31 minutes and within 30 minutes can be checked.

The goal says what to make (a print stylesheet) and where (the Larkspur Kitchen blog's recipe pages), the details say what to hide and keep, and the first criterion is checkable by printing the Barley Soup recipe to a one-page A4 PDF with the required parts present and the others absent.

The goal names the exact script and log file to change, the details name the operator and the four fields each line holds, and two criteria can be checked directly (last log line contents after success, and FAILED plus a non-zero exit when the archive cannot be written).

The goal says what to add and where (the event's time zone after the start time in Hollowbrook invitation messages to guests), the details say who it serves and what to use (the stored zone's short name), and two criteria name checkable outputs for the Berlin and New York zones.

The goal says what to add (a No articles found message and a contact form link) and where (the Driftwood help centre search results page), the details name the readers and the search box that must stay, and the zzqqxx criterion can be checked by anyone.

The goal names the exact headers and the API they go on, the details say they are for developers and that the 600-per-hour limit must not change, and the criteria can be checked by reading header values and seeing Remaining drop by one per call.

The goal names the file to write and where it goes, the details say who it is for and exactly what it must include and avoid, and the criteria on the file's contents and one-page length can be checked.
The goal names the exact text change and its place (the heading on the Thimblevane shop's About page), and the criterion that the heading reads "Our story" can be checked directly.

The goal states exactly what changes and where (Quillmoor members site idle sign-out from 15 to 60 minutes) and who it serves (members reading long articles), and the criterion that a member idle for 45 minutes is still signed in can be checked directly.

The goal says exactly what to change (the map image's alt text, with the exact wording), where (the Contact page of the Larkspur Kitchen blog) and who it is for (screen reader users), and the first criterion can be checked by looking at the image's alt attribute.

The goal names the exact change and location (rename the Hollowbrook RSVP form's Submit button to "Send my reply"), states who it is for (guests), and the build criterion that the button reads "Send my reply" can be directly seen and checked.

The goal only says to make the Driftwood help centre "better" without saying what to change, the details give no specific needs or constraints, and neither criterion ("better than before", "a reviewer agrees") names anything that can be seen or checked.

The goal only says to update the Thimblevane shop without saying what is out of date or what should change, so it could mean many different pieces of work, and neither criterion ("the shop is up to date", "a reviewer agrees") names anything that can be seen or checked.

The goal "work on the reports" does not say what is to be made or changed, so it could mean several different pieces of work, and the only checkable criterion (reports still open) cannot tell done from not done.

The goal only says to "clean up" the sign-up flow because it "feels clunky," without saying what should change, so it could mean many different pieces of work, and neither criterion lets a reviewer tell a cleaned-up flow from the current one.

The goal and details are specific enough, but no acceptance criterion can be checked, since "looks great", "readers love it" and "a reviewer agrees" are subjective and never state something observable, such as the newest recipe's photo appearing larger at the top of the home page.

The goal only says the Orders page should load faster without saying what or by how much, and every criterion ("feels faster", "staff are happier", "a reviewer agrees") is subjective with no measurable target, so a reviewer could not tell done from not done.

The goal says what to change and where, but no acceptance criterion names anything that can be seen or checked: "clearer" and "everything is good" are subjective, and the reviewer-agrees criterion gives no standard, so done cannot be told from not done.

The goal says what to make and where (a newsletter sign-up box in the Driftwood help centre footer) and who it is for, but none of the criteria names something that can be seen or checked, since "quality is high", "team is happy" and "reviewer agrees" are all subjective.

The goal only says to "improve" the weather app without naming what to change, so it could mean many different pieces of work, and neither criterion ("the app is better", "a reviewer agrees") names anything that can be seen or checked.

The goal only asks to make the Tallowmere code tidier without saying what to change or where, the details add nothing specific, and neither criterion ("code is tidier", "a reviewer agrees") names anything that can be seen or checked.

The goal "look into the members site" could mean several different pieces of work and doesn't say what to make or change, the details give no scope (only an embedded instruction, which I ignored), and neither "Things work" nor "An independent reviewer agrees" names anything that can be seen or checked.

The goal only says to do "the usual updates" to the Thimblevane shop, and the details say only "as every month", so nothing says what is to be changed and no criterion names anything a reviewer could see or check.
